# Mobile apps

## Scope

Applies when the change touches iOS, Android, cross-platform. Not when the change is a mobile-web page (`aidd-team:web-front-end`) or a desktop app (`aidd-team:desktop-apps`). Neighbours: `aidd-team:accessible-ui`, `aidd-team:release-rollout`, `aidd-team:secure-coding`, `aidd-team:privacy-by-default`.

## Dated obligations

| From | Obligation | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-04-28 | Uploads to App Store Connect are built with Xcode 26 or later and a 26 SDK. | S4 |
| 2026-08-31 | New Play apps and updates target API level 36; Wear OS and Android Automotive OS 35, Android TV and Android XR 34. | S7 |
| 2026-09-09 | iOS and iPadOS uploads target iOS 13 or later. | S4 |
| 2026-09-11 | CRA reporting applies to a commercial app (`aidd-team:incident-response`); the main obligations from 2027-12-11. | S10 |
| 2026-09-30 | Android developer verification for installs from participating stores in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand; global in 2027. | S8 |
| 2026-12-09 | Beside the CRA, the EU Product Liability Directive (EU) 2024/2853: software placed on the market after this date is a product, and a missing update can make it defective. | S10 |

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before the first edit (`aidd gate --paths`) | A store-facing change (permissions, data, SDKs, payments, sign-in, accounts, children) is major. Store review is a dependency, and the build meets the stores' dated minimums. | S2, S5, S4, S7, S8, S10 |
| Specify | Each permission with its purpose string and, for a Play restricted permission, its Play Console declaration. The privacy manifest, App Privacy, and Data safety changes as Tasks. | S3, S5, S6 |
| Specify | Digital goods through in-app purchase (3.1.1) and Play Billing; any other payment names its exception (3.1.3, physical goods, a Play exemption, or a storefront's own rule in the US, the EU, or Japan). | S2, S5 |
| Specify | Account creation brings in-app deletion (5.1.1(v)) and, on Play, a web link that deletes without the app. A social login brings an equivalent private login (4.8). | S2, S6 |
| Specify | User-generated content has filtering, reporting, blocking, and published contact (1.2); an app for children follows the Kids Category (1.3) and Play Families rules. | S2, S5 |
| Implement | Secrets in the keystore or keychain, never in the bundle; certificate pinning where MASVS requires; no sensitive data in logs or screenshots. | S1 |
| Implement | The SDK inventory is a file beside the lockfiles (SDK, version, data collected, tracking). Tracking waits for the ATT grant and, in the EU, for consent (ePrivacy Art. 5(3), `aidd-team:privacy-by-default`). Personal data sent to a third party, third-party AI included, is disclosed and consented first (5.1.2(i)). | S3, S2 |
| Implement | No hidden or dormant feature (2.3.1(a)). No downloaded code that changes features (2.5.2). A web wrapper fails 4.2, a near-copy 4.3. | S2 |
| Verify | Offline, background, interruption, and low-battery states tested on the lowest and newest OS. | S2, S7 |
| Verify | Budgets on the lowest supported device: cold start, frame time, memory, and size (Macrobenchmark, XCTest launch metrics). Crash and ANR rates stay under Play's thresholds, and memory too from February 2027; hangs show in Xcode Organizer. | S9 |
| Review | The MASVS controls, MASWE weaknesses, and MASTG cases for the change's category. | S1 |
| Roll out | Notes for Review name each new feature (2.3.1(a)) and give a working demo account or demo mode, back end on (2.1(a)). | S2 |
| Roll out | A new personal Play account runs a closed test with 12 testers for 14 days first; the pre-launch report is read before promotion. | S7 |
| Roll out | App Store phased release or a Play staged rollout, halted on the crash-free or ANR trigger. A shipped binary cannot be recalled, so a server-side switch is the rollback. | S2, S7 |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MobSF static scan | no high finding in the build | `uvx mobsfscan==1.0.1 .` on the source, MobSF on the binary | S1 |
| UI tests on the OS matrix | the flows work on every supported OS version | the `mobile-ui-test` runner in CI, on the lowest and newest OS | S2, S7 |
| Required-reason API declarations | each required-reason API the app or an SDK calls has an approved reason | the archive's symbols (`nm -u`) matched against Apple's list, diffed with `NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes` in every `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` | S3 |
| Store minimum SDK and target levels | the build meets the stores' dated minimums | bundletool 1.18.3 `dump manifest` on the AAB: `targetSdkVersion` ≥ 36; the archive's `DTSDKName` a 26 SDK, `MinimumOSVersion` ≥ 13.0 | S7, S4 |
| Sensitive permission allow-list | no permission ships undeclared or unexplained | the merged manifest (`bundletool dump manifest`) and the built Info.plist's usage-description keys against a committed allow-list | S5, S3 |
| SDK inventory against declarations | App Privacy and Data safety cover every SDK's data | a script: the lockfiles against the inventory, and the inventory against the committed App Privacy answers and Data safety export | S3, S6 |
| Account deletion end to end | in-app deletion removes the account and its data; the web link works | a UI test that signs up, deletes, and queries the API; the web deletion link checked with no session | S2, S6 |
| Review readiness smoke | the reviewer can sign in; no placeholder or dead link ships | the Notes for Review demo login against production; `lychee` (v0.24.2) over metadata and in-app URLs; a placeholder scan of strings and metadata | S2 |

- From `aidd-team:accessible-ui`: Mobile accessibility checks.

## Owned elsewhere

- Rollout stages, kill switches, and the observe window: `aidd-team:release-rollout`.
- Children's privacy law, age assurance, and the laws that make an app read the store's age signal: `aidd-team:products-for-children`.
- The European Accessibility Act, for an app sold to EU consumers: `aidd-team:accessible-ui`.

## Keep it current

Each entry is due after its `review_every_days` (else emerging 90 days, established 365) or by its `review_due`. An emerging one applies only when the change needs it, said in the Spec. One `aidd eval standards` lists as due is looked up in Specify, and a missing one is proposed to aidd's `schemas/industry-standards.json`.
